final_answer:
The sky appears blue during the day due to **Rayleigh scattering**, a phenomenon where shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) are scattered more effectively by atmospheric molecules than longer wavelengths (red, orange). Since human eyes are more sensitive to blue light and the sun emits more blue light than violet, the scattered blue light dominates our perception of the sky.

At sunset, sunlight travels through a thicker layer of the atmosphere, increasing the distance light must traverse. This causes most of the blue and green wavelengths to scatter out of the direct path, leaving the longer wavelengths (red, orange) to dominate. These colors are scattered less and thus remain visible, creating the reddish hues of sunsets. The inverse fourth-power relationship between scattering intensity and wavelength (i.e., shorter wavelengths scatter more) underpins both scenarios.
